headline: Bruins host Panthers and Pats face Packers on a busy Sunday
morning_brew: It is a massive Sunday in the Hub with two of our squads taking the field at home. The B's are back at the Garden this afternoon to host Florida, a team that has been a real thorn in our side for way too long. We have been playing some disciplined hockey, and I need the boys to bring that intensity from the opening puck drop. Getting two points against a divisional rival in our own barn would go a long way in settling some old scores, and my neighbor Rick has been pacing around the driveway since sunrise clutching an umpire dossier that is already four inches thick, swearing today is the day we finally show them who is boss.

After the hockey wraps up, we switch gears to Gillette Stadium for a late-afternoon kickoff against Green Bay. The Patriots are looking to build on the momentum they have been finding lately, and I will be watching to see how our guys match up against a team that always brings a physical fight. It is never an easy day in the NFL, but after all the noise during the week about the trade deadline, I am just ready to see our guys execute and play clean football for sixty minutes. My pops always said that games like this are won in the trenches, and if we can control the line of scrimmage, we have every chance to walk away happy.

To wrap it all up, the C's are heading out to Milwaukee tonight for a road date against the Bucks. They have been firing on all cylinders lately, playing the kind of team basketball that makes you forget all about the stress of the early season schedule. Seeing them move the ball with such confidence is a treat, and I am hopeful that they can keep that streak of high-level play moving forward in front of a hostile crowd. It is a long day of sports ahead, so grab a large iced from Dunks and buckle up, because this is exactly the kind of weekend that makes living here worth the headache.

news_digest.dans_take: The deadline chatter is heating up, and we will see if the front office actually pulls the trigger on something useful.
